<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `06f9ba5c8775f7237c03d65d3e8a644146220eaa` — the merge of head `8d7a02d5a906dd2c108f015c92d9cab68cc25c14` into base `40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 06f9ba5c8775f7237c03d65d3e8a644146220eaa && git checkout 06f9ba5c8775f7237c03d65d3e8a644146220eaa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15 8d7a02d5a906dd2c108f015c92d9cab68cc25c14 && git checkout -B drift-repro 40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15 && git merge --no-ff 8d7a02d5a906dd2c108f015c92d9cab68cc25c14

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 40fa433539cba010343b02ede4e66cccfab47d15` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d1809dd5f313da03290528b631c0cab33b9c9baa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `.changeset/29898-picklist-binding-unknown-refused.md` · `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.picklist-binding-unknown-refused.ts` (against siblings `17.datasource-config-url-userinfo-refused.ts`, `entries/README.md`, `migrations/types.ts`) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` (new judge, and the precedents `unknownGrantObjectSaveRefusal` #28990 / `unknownDatasourceSaveRefusal` #26724) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (`saveMetaItem` call site ~L14711, `promoteDraftForPublish` ~L16700, the private method + docblock, the restore docblock, `writeSource` derivation L13531, the three internal `saveMetaItem` callers: migrate-stored L15828, `duplicatePackage` L19188, unmanaged import L19407) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts` (`restoredBodyWriter`, `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts` (what `readMetaItem` answers for an `object`) · `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts` · `packages/metadata/src/picklist-references.ts` (`collectPicklistReferences`) · `packages/objectql/src/picklist-resolution.ts` · `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`resolvePicklistOptions`, `picklistContributions`, `findUnresolvedPicklistReferences`, `getItem`/`getObject`) · `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (boot audit sites) · `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:932` (`picklist` type entry) · `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts` · the four test files in the diff (`protocol.unknown-picklist-binding-refusal.test.ts`, `protocol.restore-doors-save-refusal-family.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-picklist-binding-door.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.boot-parity.test.ts`) · `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` hunk · `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (marker grammar) · `scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` (header) · sibling changesets `29904-type-mismatch-fail-closed.md` (#29923) and `sec-hardening-g-external-object-organization-scope.md` · `AGENTS.md` Post-Task Checklist · `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md` · card #29898 + comments 6601945270, 6608538627 · PR #29956 body, files, check-runs.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset) + published spec path. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Accept-set narrows at five doors, as declared.** `saveMetaItem` (draft and publish mode, every `writeSource` but `migrate-stored`), `promoteDraftForPublish` (the per-item publish and, through it, `publishPackageDrafts`), and both restore doors via `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`. Each body of type `object` or `object_extension` whose field names a picklist the engine's registry does not resolve, and which the object does not already hold on that field, is refused `422 INVALID_METADATA`. Correct: the PR body, the changeset and the D3 entry name the same five doors. Nothing is widened — no new key, value or type is accepted; the method is `private`, so the published `.d.ts` surface of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` gains nothing (`Clause-②: no` holds).
- **"Declared" is the serve path's own predicate.** `resolvePicklistOptions(name) !== undefined` is exactly what `resolvePicklistFields` uses to serve a bound field's options and what the boot audit `findUnresolvedPicklistReferences` uses (registry.ts L8473). `picklistContributions` reads `getItem('picklist', name)` with the registry's bare/prefer-local/first-composite fallback, so the list is resolved by name across every package installed here: the package's own, a dependency's, a `.custom` pair's base, and an unrelated installed package all resolve. The door therefore cannot refuse a list the field would be served. Correct, and pinned over the real `SchemaRegistry` + sqlite in `meta-picklist-binding-door.test.ts` (dependency, `.custom` base, same-env non-dependency each saved, published and served its options).
- **Boot ordering is not reachable by this judge.** Code packages register through `registerApp`/`registerPlugin`, never through `saveMetaItem`; `protocol-package-install.ts` calls no `saveMetaItem`; the boot audit stays the authority for a package's own objects. The save door is reached only by runtime writes after the boot sealed (REST/Studio, `migrate-stored` [exempt], `duplicatePackage`, unmanaged import, restores). A registry that lacks `resolvePicklistOptions` refuses nothing (the `getObject` posture of #28990). Correct.
- **No pending arm is right.** `picklist` is `allowRuntimeCreate: false`, `supportsOverlay: false` (metadata-plugin.zod.ts:932): no draft of any batch can declare one, so "the same package's draft picklist saved later" cannot exist, and the ordering trap the datasource/grant judges needed a `pending` arm for does not arise. A draft bound to a list no installed package declares is refused at the draft save — the card's step 2 expectation, and the only way to make the list resolvable is to install a code package, after which the same save passes.
- **Held-binding exemption.** Keyed on the `[field, picklist]` pair read from the object's current definition (`readMetaItem({type:'object'})`: stored active row, else artifact, else `registry.getObject`, which folds `extend` contributors). A renamed field, a new field, and a re-bind of a held field to another unknown list are each a new pair and are refused — pinned (`qa_old` cases). A draft is not "held" (a planted pre-rule draft re-saved is refused — pinned). `migrate-stored` is exempt by `writeSource` and would be held anyway for active rows. Bypass-free as far as I can derive. One edge not pinned: an `object_extension` re-save on a STORED (runtime-package) base object — step 1 of `readMetaItem` answers the base's stored row, which does not carry the extension's fields, so an extension holding a binding on a list gone since could be refused on re-save. For the designed case (a `.custom` extension on a code base) the registry fold covers it. Low reach; observation, not a blocker.
- **Side effect the body does not state:** `duplicatePackage` (L19188) and the unmanaged import (L19407) copy items through `saveMetaItem(mode: 'publish')` with no exemption, and the copy target holds nothing yet, so a source object holding a binding on a list gone since is now refused when copied (the import rolls back). This is the same property `unknownGrantObjectSaveRefusal` already gives those two paths, and the refusal is correct on the merits (the copy would be served with no options). Should be named in the PR body's Acceptance notes; not a defect.
- **Message:** `Field '<object>.<field>' is bound to picklist '<list>', which no loaded package declares, so the field would be served with no options …` + three remedies (correct the name / declare the list in a code package / inline `options`), at `path: fields.<field>.picklist`, `code: 'custom'`, in the schema-gate envelope `<type>/<name> failed spec validation: …`. For an extension the object named is the one extended. Names the field, the list and the fix. Correct; pinned by first sentence and path at every door.
- **One inaccurate derived claim.** The PR body ("the one shared walk … the boot audit's and the `os validate` door's"), the new CLI source comment ("over the same walk") and the dev report say the CLI judge shares `collectPicklistReferences`. It does not: `packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts` walks the parsed artifact with its own `referencesOf`; only its residual half reads `@objectstack/metadata`. The save door and the BOOT AUDIT share the walk (true); the CLI agrees by pin, not by inheritance — which the parity test's own header states correctly. A prose/comment error, no behaviour rides on it.
- **`packages/spec`:** the D3 entry is the only change; `FieldSchema.picklist` and every Zod shape are untouched; the refusal is a door judgement against the registry (environment-dependent), which a schema cannot express. The order's stop condition is respected.

### ② Semver level
`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` ⇒ `minor` on every package the diff moves. The changeset bumps `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/cli` `minor` — the three publishable packages the diff touches (`packages/runtime` and `scripts/` carry test/ledger files only, which publish nothing; the `fixed` group versions them together regardless). `cli` moves by one source comment, so `minor` there is over-declared but is the letter of the rule and harmless. Summary line `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`, both declaration lines line-initial, exactly one ADR-0087 marker `<!-- adr-0087: registered picklist-binding-unknown-refused -->` whose id matches the D3 entry's `id` and filename `18.<id>.ts` (spec is `18.2.0`; README naming rule met; no index to edit; `registry.ts` is generated and gitignored, so nothing else to commit). `**BREAKING**` banner, Before/Now/Unchanged, FROM → TO with the one-line fix — the same shape as the #29923 precedent (`29904-type-mismatch-fail-closed.md`). `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on this head. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`); PR is a draft; no extra-author note owed.
- CI at review time: every completed check green (`Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`), zero failures; `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8)`, `Test UI (1–16)`, `Type Check · workspace/consumer/debt`, `Lint · repo & tooling` / `scoped · slot lookup` still `in_progress`. The seat's own ② landing check (全绿) is still owed on completion.
- Dev flag "measured surface shift: lint → metadata-protocol": upheld. `validateObjectReferences` runs on `runtimeTypes: ['flow','dataset']`, the CLI judge is deliberately not a lint registry rule (its header says why), and `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` is where this family lives (#26724, #28990). No `packages/lint` file is touched, so no overlap with #29926.
- Dev flag "CLI vs save-door divergence" (a list owned by an installed package that is neither in the artifact nor a declared dependency: CLI `error`/`info`, save door accepts): acceptable to leave. The save door is bound to the serve path and must accept; the CLI reads one artifact and cannot see the environment, and a stack that depends on an installed package without declaring the dependency is a stack defect the CLI is right to name — the author's fix is to declare the dependency, after which the CLI downgrades to the `info` notice. No card required; the divergence is recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes and in the CLI header. If the seat wants it on the ledger, a p4 devx note is enough.
- Ablation coverage: only the `saveMetaItem` call site was ablated (8 red / 7 green, the 7 being the promote pins and controls). The promote and restore arms were not ablated. By construction they are load-bearing for their pins: the planted-draft publish pins bypass the save door entirely (rows planted into the double), and `restoredBodyWriter` runs its own refusal chain and never enters `saveMetaItem`, so nothing else in either path reads a picklist — remove the arm and the pin must go green-publish → red. The order's "each negative pin ablated once" is nonetheless two legs short in measured form; see follow-ups.
- `Skills-docs:` line is on the PR body (`no move`) but not in the changeset body; the order's wording admits either reading, no gate reads it, and the #29923 precedent changeset omits it too. Not blocking.
- PR body says repo-wide `pnpm lint` was "left to CI"; the dev report says it ran green after the PR opened. The seat should correct that line when appending the trailer.

### ④ Narrowing face
- `protocol-save-door-refusals.ts` / `protocol.ts`: the judge follows `unknownGrantObjectSaveRefusal`'s shape (registry first, then the held definition), is asked at the same position in `saveMetaItem` as its siblings (after the schema gate, before the authoring gate and every write), under the same `migrate-stored` exemption, at `promoteDraftForPublish` on the draft body before `repo.promoteDraft` (so a batch aborts), and in the restore chain. The envelope and `issues[]` shape are the schema gate's. Holds against the card's acceptance scenario (steps 2–5: the PUT is refused, nothing is stored, nothing publishes) and against the three "declared" controls the ruling section required (dependency, `.custom` base, same-env installed), each pinned over a real registry.
- `18.picklist-binding-unknown-refused.ts`: `id`/`surface`/`replacement`/`reason`/`acceptanceCriteria` populated in the siblings' register; `surface` names the doors and the field key, `replacement` the three remedies, `reason` why there is no mechanical rewrite, `acceptanceCriteria` a verifiable loop (save → publish → GET serves options → data write 200). No `conversionIds` (none applies). The entry's first consumer is the upgrade guide; no executor needed.
- Changeset FROM → TO reads as the prescription an upgrading agent greps: `picklist: 'nope_list'` → a declared list, or declare it in a code package, or inline `options`. Matches the refusal text and the D3 `replacement`.
- Pins cover: four save modes (draft+package, draft, publish, `force`), `multiselect`, `object_extension`, planted pre-rule draft at `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts` (batch refused, nothing promoted), a list gone between save and publish, `migrate-stored` exempt then publish refused, re-save of a bad draft refused, held binding kept while new/renamed/re-bound fields refused, registry without `resolvePicklistOptions`, both restore doors with controls, the two-judge parity (sibling-owned list accepted by both; typo refused by both at the same field tail). Adequate for the narrowing face.

### ① Derived judgments
